_doubling_note: 艾娃 + 娃 = 娃娃, 莱拉 + 拉 = 拉拉拉, 拉拉 + 拉 = 拉拉拉, 凯尔 + 尔 and 米卡 + 卡 are both ordinary words. The rule only fires on the literal "term + term's last character" shape, so listing the canonical spelling here is enough to exempt it; the checker does not try to tell these apart from a doubled typo.
_kept_verbatim_note: 105 distinct strings, 273 occurrences, none of them prose. They fall into four groups. (1) Interpolation and punctuation only -- 124 occurrences of "???" for the protagonist's silent or masked lines, plus "[sophia]...", "[r1]?", "▸", "?" and friends: there is no word to translate. (2) Ren'Py Preference keys -- "text speed", "music volume", "sound volume", "voice volume", "all mute", "after choices", "auto-forward": these are looked up by name, and the visible label beside each one is translated (screens.rpy:802 label _("文字显示速度")). (3) Identifiers the engine matches on -- "Q.Save" was one of these too and is now translated, while "bio_MC", "LI_info_page2", "phoneFrame", "notifyEx", "dialogueBoxOpacity", "MC", "bio_MC" and "DropOutSaga" remain, because they name screens, images, persistent keys or the save directory. (4) In-world lines the game itself leaves in another language -- "Gut.", "Kazhetsya, eto zdes'", "Mein vater wanted a son.", "An American Language!", "Jaz...": translating these would change what the scene is doing. One deliberate stylistic variant is NOT in this list: script.rpy:993 renders Lila's name as 「莉、莉拉」 because the English has her say it with a stutter ("Lee-lah?"), and 艾娃's own list would flag it, so it is called out here instead.
_coverage_note: Coverage is measured, not asserted. The extraction pass found 15,214 translatable literals in the English release; 14,941 are Chinese in the patch and the 273 above are verbatim, which adds up exactly. tools/verify_patch.py re-derives both numbers from data/coverage.json and fails if either moves.
